'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Eastern front of the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Eastern Ukraine offensive]]
****[[Siege of Mariupol]]
*****A [[Russia]]n [[airstrike]] destroys a [[maternity ward]] and a [[children's hospital]] in [[Mariupol]], [[Ukraine]], killing three people and injuring at least 17 people. President [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says that many people are unaccounted for. [https://www.businessinsider.com/zelenskyy-condemns-russia-direct-strike-at-mariupol-maternity-hospital-2022-3 (''Business Insider'')] [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-kyiv-europe-2bed71c00916d44ea951c5809b446db3 (AP)] [https://www.chicagotribune.com/nation-world/ct-aud-nw-russia-ukraine-war-20220309-q3hazn6ei5aqxcyaytfwxmlgue-story.html (''The Chicago Tribune'')] [https://news.sky.com/story/ukraine-war-children-buried-under-rubble-after-russian-airstrike-hit-hospital-in-mariupol-president-zelenskyy-says-12561747 (Sky News)]
****[[Battle of Kharkiv (2022)|Battle of Kharkiv]]
*****[[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] announce that they have regained control of [[Derhachi]], a city located in the [[Kharkiv Raion]] district of the [[Kharkiv Oblast]]. [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3425090-ukraine-army-regains-control-over-kharkiv-regions-derhachi.html (Ukrinform)] 
***[[Ukrainian refugee crisis]]
****The [[United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees]] says over two million [[Ukrainians]] have now fled the country since the invasion began. Most have gone to neighbouring [[Poland]], with [[Hungary]], [[Romania]] and [[Slovakia]] also taking in several hundred thousand refugees each. [https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-number-of-refugees-reaches-2-million-un-says/a-61048556 (DW)]
***[[Poland–United States relations]]
****[[The Pentagon]] rejects an offer from [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Poland)|Poland's foreign ministry]] to "deploy – immediately and free of charge – all their [[Mikoyan MiG-29|MIG-29]] jets" to the [[Ramstein Air Base]] and place them at the disposal of the Government of the [[United States of America]]" for transfer to the [[Ukrainian Air Force]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-surprised-polands-decision-give-it-fighter-jets-ukraine-2022-03-08/ (Reuters)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/poland-ready-place-all-its-mig-29-jets-disposal-us-2022-03-08/ (Reuters 2)] 
***[[Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
****The [[British Army]] confirms that a number of active-duty soldiers have disobeyed orders and gone [[AWOL]], and have likely gone to Ukraine to fight against the [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian military]]. Defence Minister [[Ben Wallace (politician)|Ben Wallace]] says that the serving members are "breaking the law and will be prosecuted" when they return to the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/ukraine-war-british-army-confirms-a-number-of-soldiers-have-gone-awol-and-may-have-travelled-to-fight-russia-12561964 (Sky News)]
****The [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)|Defence Ministry]] says that it is sending another 1,615 [[Next generation Light Anti-tank Weapon|MBT LAWs]], and a small number of [[FGM-148 Javelin]] [[Anti-tank warfare|anti-tank missiles]] to the [[Ukrainian Ground Forces|Ukrainian army]]. More small arms, body armour and medical supplies have also been sent. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-60679658 (BBC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Fitch Ratings]] downgrades Russia from "B" to "C", one grade above default, and warns that Russian default on its obligations is "imminent". [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-60672085 (BBC News)]
***The [[Ministry of Economic Development (Russia)|Russian Ministry of Economic Development]] proposes a draft [[nationalisation]] bill that will impose [[receivership]] for up to 3 months on assets of companies that boycotted the Russian market due to the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]] if the ownership share by legal entities from "unfriendly countries" exceeds 25%. If the companies still do not resume their business in the country, their assets will be auctioned. More than 300 companies that left Russia or suspended operations in Russia could be targeted. [https://tass.ru/ekonomika/14016049 (TASS)]
**[[Boycott of Russia and Belarus]]
***[[Governor of New Jersey|New Jersey Governor]] [[Phil Murphy]] signs a legislation banning [[New Jersey|the state]] from doing business dealings with [[Belarus]] and [[Russia]]. [https://patch.com/new-jersey/across-nj/new-jersey-bans-state-business-dealings-russia-belarus (Patch.com)]
***[[John Deere]] announces that it will suspend shipments to Russia and Belarus following the invasion. [https://www.wbtv.com/2022/03/09/john-deere-suspends-shipments-russia-belarus/ (WBTV-TV)]
***American industrial [[conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] [[3M]] suspends all business operations in Russia. [https://www.reuters.com/article/ukraine-crisis-3m/3m-suspends-business-in-russia-idUKL3N2VC3VV (Reuters)]
**The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China|Chinese Foreign Ministry]] announces that [[China]] will provide 5 million [[Yuan (currency)|yuan]] ([[United States dollar|$]]790,000) in humanitarian aid to Ukraine. [https://amp.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3169853/china-sends-first-shipment-humanitarian-aid-ukraine (''South China Morning Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**The Ukrainian state grid operator warns that Russian forces, which are in control of the [[Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant]], have disconnected the plant from the electricity grid, which the operator says will impact nuclear fuel cooling, and which also caused a blackout in the nearby city of [[Slavutych]]. The nuclear plant previously suspended all communications with the [[IAEA]], the [[United Nations]]-based organisation specialising in nuclear energy production. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/ukraine-chernobyl-nuclear-power-plant-outage-b2031874.html (''The Independent'')] [https://ua.interfax.com.ua/news/general/810021.html (Interfax Ukraine)]
**Ukrainian Foreign Minister [[Dmytro Kuleba]] says that reserve diesel generators that cool [[spent nuclear fuel]] can only last for another 48 hours and that a [[radiation]] leak from Chernobyl is "imminent" if power is not restored immediately. Kuleba also says that "[[Vladimir Putin|Putin]]'s barbaric war" puts all of Europe in danger. However, the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] says there is "no critical impact on security" imminent. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/ukraine-warns-48-hours-until-radiation-leaks-after-power-lost-at-chernobyl/ (''Times of Israel'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/ukraine-nuclear-firm-warns-radiation-risk-after-power-cut-occupied-chernobyl-2022-03-09/ (Reuters)]
*[[2022 eastern Australia floods]]
**[[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] declares a national emergency in [[Australia]] in response to the ongoing floods in Australia. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-03-09/scott-morrison-floods-national-emergency-funding-billions/100894056 (ABC News Australia)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Austria]]
****[[Austria]] suspends its universal COVID-19 [[vaccine mandate]] one week before fines of up to €3,600 were scheduled to take effect for those who did not comply with the mandate. The suspension of the mandate will be reviewed in three months. [https://www.politico.eu/article/austria-suspends-coronavirus-vaccine-mandate/ (''Politico'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]
****[[Romania]] lifts all COVID-19-related restrictions including requiring a digital COVID pass to access institutions and the obligation to wear protective masks both indoors and outdoors. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/romanian-government-lift-covid-restrictions-march-9-2022-03-08/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
***[[South Korea]] reports a record 342,446 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 Hours. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/covid-19-south-korea-new-cases-record-mar-9-2550231 (CNA)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***[[Russia–United States relations]]
****[[Government of Russia|Kremlin]] spokesman [[Dmitry Peskov]] tells the [[United States]] to "await its response" to the "economic war" being waged against [[Russia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/russia-warns-west-our-sanctions-will-hurt-you-2022-03-09/ (Reuters)]
***[[Russia–United Kingdom relations]]
****The [[United Kingdom|UK]] bans all Russian aircraft from landing in its territory and travelling in its airspace, impounding a [[Russian oligarch]]-owned [[private jet]] at [[Farnborough Airport]]. The UK also bans all exports of aviation and [[space industry of Russia|space industry]]-related goods and services. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/britain-announces-new-aviation-sanctions-against-russia-2022-03-09/ (Reuters)]
**[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
***[[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Russia)|Russian Foreign Minister]] [[Sergey Lavrov]] arrives in [[Ankara]], [[Turkey]], for upcoming talks with [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Ukraine)|Ukrainian Foreign Minister]] [[Dmytro Kuleba]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/russias-lavrov-arrives-turkey-talks-with-ukraine-counterpart-2022-03-09/ (Reuters)]
***Ukrainian foreign policy aide Ihor Zhovkva says that [[Ukraine]] is open to holding talks discussing Russia's demand of Ukraine's neutrality as long as Ukraine is given security guarantees. However, Zhovkva warned that Ukraine will not give up any of its territories. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-03-09/ukraine-open-to-neutrality-but-won-t-yield-territory-aide-says (Bloomberg)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 South Korean presidential election]]
**Preliminary results of the presidential election show a narrow victory for the conservative candidate [[Yoon Suk-yeol]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/live/2022/03/08/world/korean-election (''The New York Times'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*The wreck of [[Ernest Shackleton]]'s ship ''[[Endurance (1912 ship)|Endurance]]'', which sank in 1915, has been located beneath the [[Weddell Sea]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/03/09/climate/endurance-wreck-found-shackleton.html (''The New York Times'')]
